newsitem.title: USA: Senior U.S. trade negotiator leaving.
newsitem.headline: Senior U.S. trade negotiator leaving.

text.p: Senior U.S. trade negotiator Ira Shapiro said on Sunday that he planned to leave the Clinton administration early this year.
Shapiro said in an interview that he told U.S. Trade Representative-designate Charlene Barshefsky in December that he would probably be leaving within a few months.
"I wanted to make sure when she thought about her team that she would know that I wasn't going to be there," Shapiro said.
He did not specify a departure date, nor did he say what he would be doing.
"I'm going to move on to new challenges, one of which is paying college tuition," he said. He has two teenage children.
As senior counsel and negotiator at the U.S. Trade Representative's Office, Shapiro has been an important figure in trade talks with Japan, Canada and Mexico.
